relevance_note: Case report of an infant and her father carrying a TNFAIP3 nonsense variant: 'The variant was confirmed by Sanger sequencing in the infant and her father.'
method_note: Hand-built JSON with a small Python script in scratch; all values read from the paper by hand. Four people in scope: the infant ('patient', single unnamed case-report patient, called 'the proband' in Fig. 2), her father (TNFAIP3 carrier, affected), her mother (described in relation to the infant; autoantibody tests negative, not genetically tested) and her grandmother (affected, side of family not stated, not tested). Father's variant row records only 'c.492G>A' as printed in the Fig. 2 legend; zygosity, type and pathogenicity not stated for him and left not reported (v5 rule). NF1 variant recorded for the infant as WES finding attributed to her; variant type not stated. Contradiction: Case description calls the TNFAIP3 variant 'a definite pathogenic mutation' (abstract: 'pathogenic variant'), but the Discussion says 'likely pathogenic variant nonsense mutations'; the case-description wording is recorded. MutationTaster and conservation scores are in-silico predictions and the authors state no functional study was done, so functional evidence is not reported. Age at last evaluation taken from the last column of Table 2 (20 mon). C3/C4 values have no reference range or 'low' wording, so low complement is not recorded. 'Her latest laboratory tests (Table 1)' conflicts with Table 1 being initial tests; not used. Discussion's 'did not have arthritis, bloody diarrhea, or ocular inflammation' excludes ocular inflammation but not arthralgia or GI inflammation (narrow vs broad). No stacked cells.
